newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker, outperform U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker, outperform U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker on Tuesday, but outperformed their U.S. counterparts, as a stronger Canadian dollar partially offset the pressure of upcoming U.S. and Canadian supply, analysts said.

"The story remains the same. The Canadian dollar was very bullish this morning. We saw European buying of Canada," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed-income research with ABN-AMRO Bank Canada. "That all factors into the outperformance of Canada over the U.S."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.38 to C$111.00 to yield 7.070 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 16/32 to yield 6.92 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 15 basis points from 18 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.
Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets opened weaker this morning ahead of auctions today and tomorrow.
The U.S. Treasury this afternoon will auction US$17 billion of three year notes as part of its quarterly refunding, and tomorrow will auction US$12 billion in 10-year notes.
The Canadian government on Wednesday will auction C$2.4 billion in 10-year bonds.

Analysts said Canadian bonds weakened as many investors sold to lock in recent gains ahead of the supply. The Canadian fixed-income market has closed stronger for five consecutive sessions. But helping to limits gains was the stronger dollar.

Canada's dollar opened stronger at C$1.3771 (US$0.7261) in light trading on Tuesday. Dealers said the currency's strength was based on a decline in speculation that U.S. rates will rise and expectations of a market-friendly Ontario budget.
"This type of (bond market) outperformance we're seeing right now I think could be shortlived if the currency reverses," Pyle said.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bonds fell C$0.22 to C$103.38 to yield 6.519 percent. The U.S. bond fell 11/32 to yield 6.70 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 18 basis points from 17 basis points on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.99 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.18 percent.
